candidates.title: PagedMoE: Cross-Precision Expert Caching for Token-Level Dynamic Precision in SSD-Resident MoE Inference
candidates.abstract: Large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are promising for local inference because sparse routing allows the routed-expert pool to reside on SSD while DRAM caches recently used experts. However, under practical DRAM cache capacities, substantial SSD I/O remains on the critical path despite I/O-computation overlap. Token-level dynamic expert precision offers a natural way to reduce this data demand by allocating bits according to expert importance and quantization sensitivity. Nevertheless, treating each bit-width of the same expert as an independent object prevents cross-precision cache reuse, causing overlapping data to be fetched repeatedly. The key insight is that precision should instead denote the refinement depth of one shared expert state. Based on this insight, we present PagedMoE, which stores each expert once using a prefix-compatible tree codebook and bitplane layout. Lower-precision representations are valid prefixes of higher-precision ones, allowing cached data to be reused or extended by fetching only missing bitplanes. PagedMoE selects the required prefix length before I/O using current routing weights and offline expert-specific error profiles, and directly executes cached 1-8-bit prefixes without materializing full-precision experts. At an average routed-expert precision of 2.5 bits, PagedMoE achieves quality close to GPTQ-INT4 on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and to MXFP4 on most evaluated GLM5.2 tasks. With a 24 GiB expert cache, it reaches 8.89 tokens/s on Qwen3.5, 1.33x the throughput of the same dynamic requests using independent precision objects and 1.56x that of uniform 4-bit execution.
candidates.reason: PagedMoEはSSD常駐MoE推論で、精度を共有エキスパート状態の精緻化深さとして扱う接頭辞互換ツリーコードブックとビットプレーン配置により、トークン単位の動的精度でも低精度表現を高精度の接頭辞として再利用し、DRAMキャッシュからのSSD I/Oを削減するエキスパートキャッシュ機構である。

candidates.title: CIM for Transformer Models: Enhancing Large Language Model Inference Efficiency
candidates.venue: IEEE Computer Society Annual Symposium on VLSI
candidates.abstract: In the field of large language model (LLM) inference, the high computational demand and extensive memory requirements for weights and key-value (KV) cache storage present significant challenges. This issue becomes especially problematic when relying exclusively on GPUs, as they often lack the capacity to accommodate the entire KV cache, particularly in larger LLMs. In the absence of direct communications like NVlink among multiple GPUs, LLMs typically require offloading the KV cache to the CPU for storage and computation, followed by transferring the multi-head attention results back to the GPU for subsequent transformer computations. Given that attention score computation is computationally demanding on the CPU and requires substantial data movement between KV caches and memory, the direct computation of attention scores and even the feedforward layers on Compute-in-Memory (CIM) systems emerges as a viable alternative. This paper is at the forefront of integrating CIM technology in LLM inference, and proposes an innovative architecture that leverages this emerging technology to enhance inference efficiency. Specifically, we present a tailored CIM-based dataflow and hierarchy design for optimize the computation of attention scores and feed-forward layers using CIMs. The results show improvements in performance, with $0.026 \times$ inference latency and $1.199 \times 10^{-3} \times$ energy as compared to a CPU-based implementation.
candidates.reason: GPUだけでは重みとKVキャッシュを収めきれないLLM推論に対し、KVキャッシュをCPUへオフロードする代わりに注意スコア計算やフィードフォワード層までCompute-in-Memory上で直接計算し、データ移動と計算のボトルネックを解くCIM統合を提案しており、LLM推論ハードウェアに直接貢献する。

candidates.title: Enabling Software-Defined Tiered LLM Inference Continuum on Passive Optical Network
candidates.abstract: The rapid expansion of large language models (LLMs) has shifted inference workloads from centralized cloud servers toward distributed execution across fog and edge environments. As this trend accelerates, existing broadband infrastructures, particularly passive optical networks (PONs), must evolve to meet the stringent latency, bandwidth, and coordination demands of real-time LLM inference. Therefore, it is essential to enhance the access network with intelligence and programmability to support efficient, scalable, and low-latency inference delivery across multiple network layers. This paper presents a software-defined architecture for enabling tiered LLM inference over Time and Wavelength Division Multiplexed Passive Optical Networks (TWDM-PON). The proposed system incorporates LLM-integrated Optical Line Terminals (OLTs) and Optical Network Units (ONUs), each equipped with processing and queuing capabilities to execute portions of LLM inference tasks locally. These intelligent nodes collaborate under centralized Software-Defined Networking (SDN) control to manage inference-related traffic and optimize resource allocation across the network. Through inference-aware dynamic bandwidth allocation, time and wavelength slicing, and queue-level traffic isolation, the architecture prioritizes LLM traffic to provide low and consistent latency for LLM inference tasks for prompt and token streams without degrading conventional broadband services. Simulation results show that the proposed architecture reduces average inference latency by up to 50%, improves throughput by up to 7%, and lowers jitter and packet drop probability by up to 32% and 25.01%, respectively, while maintaining end-to-end Quality of Service (QoS) under mixed broadband and LLM traffic.
candidates.reason: TWDM受動光ネットワーク上にソフトウェア定義の階層型LLM推論基盤を構築し、処理・キューイング機能を持つOLT／ONU等のインテリジェント光ノードへ推論タスクを分散配置して低レイテンシな推論配信を実現するアーキテクチャであり、分散LLM推論の実行基盤に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: BlockFormer: An Efficient Private Batch Transformer Inference With Homomorphic Encryption via Block Packing
candidates.abstract: Although transformer models have established a new paradigm for today’s language processing, regulatory compliance in machine learning as a service remains essential due to the involvement of sensitive data. Several homomorphic encryption (HE)-based approaches for privacy-preserving transformer inference (PPTI) exist; however, their performance remains suboptimal due to limited support for scalable batching and reliance on complex approximations of non-linear functions. In this paper, we propose BlockFormer, an efficient batch PPTI solution that employs a novel Block Packing (BP) strategy, supporting a wide range of batch sizes and input lengths. Compared to the state-of-the-art HE-based batch PPTI approach, MOAI (Zhang et al., ICLR’26), which is efficient only for a specific, relatively large batch size, BlockFormer overcomes this limitation and mitigates the exponential growth in runtime as the batch size decreases, thereby enabling its use across a broader range of application scenarios. Moreover, BlockFormer leverages lower-degree polynomial approximations for non-linear functions, including GELU and Softmax, compared with Powerformer (Park et al., ACL’25), thereby further reducing evaluation complexity. To preserve model accuracy, knowledge distillation is applied during retraining. Evaluations demonstrate the superior efficiency of BlockFormer on the BERT-base model. At a batch size of 4, BlockFormer achieves a <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$28.3\times $ </tex-math></inline-formula> performance improvement over MOAI and is <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$2.3\times $ </tex-math></inline-formula> faster than Powerformer at a batch size of 256. Compared to the multi-party computation-based approach BOLT (Pang et al., S&P’24), under the batch size of 256, BlockFormer is <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$3.5\times $ </tex-math></inline-formula> faster per sample at 100 Mbps bandwidth and reduces communication overhead by approximately <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$600\times $ </tex-math></inline-formula>. Overall, our solution attains the highest accuracy among related works, achieving 93.4% on the SST-2 dataset and 70.7% on the RTE dataset. To demonstrate the generality of our packing technique, we further evaluate BlockFormer on a LLaMA-3-8B-scaled configuration, achieving up to a <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$121\times $ </tex-math></inline-formula> speedup.
candidates.reason: BlockFormerは準同型暗号によるプライバシー保護Transformer推論で、ブロックパッキング戦略により多様なバッチサイズと入力長へ対応し、従来のバッチ型PPTIが小バッチで指数的に悪化する実行時間を抑える効率的なバッチ私的推論方式であり、機密推論の実行機構に直接貢献する。

candidates.title: Aggressive Post-Training Compression on Extremely Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of Large Language Models (LLMs) pose challenges for their deployment on personal computers and mobile devices. Aggressive post-training model compression is necessary to reduce the models' size, but it often results in significant accuracy loss. To address this challenge, we propose a novel network pruning technology that utilizes over 0.7 sparsity and less than 8 bits of quantization. Our approach enables the compression of prevailing LLMs within a couple of hours while maintaining a relatively small accuracy loss. In experimental evaluations, our method demonstrates effectiveness and potential for practical deployment. By making LLMs available on domestic devices, our work can facilitate a new era of natural language processing applications with wide-ranging impacts.
candidates.reason: 0.7超の疎性と8ビット未満の量子化を組み合わせた積極的な学習後圧縮で、巨大LLMを数時間で圧縮し精度損失を小さく抑えてPCやモバイル等の家庭用デバイスへ配備可能にする技術であり、LLMの配備向け圧縮に直接貢献する。
